title: Infinite Space
subtitle: A life measured in star systems
summary: Infinite Space is Nude Maker and PlatinumGames' Nintendo DS science-fiction role-playing game following Yuri from a young traveller into the command of a growing fleet. body: Infinite Space is Nude Maker and PlatinumGames' Nintendo DS science-fiction role-playing game following Yuri from a young traveller into the command of a growing fleet. His journey crosses the Small and Large Magellanic Clouds and becomes entangled in conflicts far larger than his original ambition. Ships and crew are customisable, while dialogue and decisions shape parts of the route and the people who join. The portable format carries an unusually broad space opera, using the organisation of a fleet to connect personal growth with the scale of interstellar events.

The player travels between planets and issues commands in real-time ship battles rather than directly steering an individual craft. Choosing ships, arranging their capabilities and assigning crew therefore has consequences once an encounter begins. The touchscreen handles the selection of destinations and orders, giving the adventure the feel of directing activity from a command interface. A successful fleet needs more than a collection of impressive hulls. Its preparation has to support the actions available during a fight and the sequence in which those orders can be used.

Crew fatigue increases during travel and reduces efficiency, while stopping at a port restores the fleet and its people. The journey is consequently a sequence of departures and necessary returns to inhabited places. Decisions can also determine which characters join Yuri, making the growing organisation part of the story's response to the player. Static illustrated conversations and three-dimensional travel or battles operate at different scales. Infinite Space uses that contrast to keep the people visible inside a game whose most immediate symbols of progress are large spacecraft and distant destinations.
